steps.title: KGA, plant and replay on the original PPSEB

kga.method: public PEKS.Encrypt + Verify against the captured token

trace.title: Threat model: the doctor's trapdoor is a blockchain transaction
trace.detail: PPSEB moves the search step on-chain for auditability: the doctor submits Trap as a transaction so a consensus node can run Verify. That means every node (and any observer of the chain) sees Trap in the clear — no compromise of the doctor's device is needed.

trace.title: Why this works: PEKS.Encrypt and Verify are both PUBLIC algorithms
trace.detail: PEKS.Encrypt(pk_rj, guess, j) needs no secret at all (that's the point of a public-key scheme: anyone can encrypt). Verify(CT, Trap) needs no secret either. An attacker can therefore re-encrypt every dictionary word exactly as the real sender would, and test each one against the captured trapdoor exactly as the real search node would.

trace.title: Seal and deliver the capability to doctor_c
